subject: Mid-cycle surge: flexible billing and uplift options
messages:
From: Alex Harper <alex@brightwave.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected usage spike — options for mid-cycle billing?

Hi Stephanie,

Quick note from our side — we hit a traffic surge last week for our customer-facing feature and burned ~2.8x of our expected token volume. We’re only a month into the quarter and the committed capacity on our contract isn’t enough to cover the run rate.

Can you outline what paths you can offer mid-cycle so we can get coverage without waiting until renewal? Specifically looking for:
- short-term uplift (one-off top-up vs temporary buffer)
- how discounts would reapply if we annualize now vs true-up later
- any billing smoothing so we don't get hit with a big invoice that messes up our month-end commitments

We can share the usage CSV if helpful — happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Alex Harper
Head of Platform
BrightWave AI

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Harper <alex@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike — options for mid-cycle billing?

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and the context. We can definitely offer a few practical approaches; I’ll summarize options and the trade-offs so you can pick what fits BrightWave’s cash flow and procurement needs. Attaching a short usage snapshot you mentioned.

Options (high-level):
1) Temporary top-up (one-off invoice)
   - Adds capacity for the remainder of this quarter only.
   - No change to discount tiering. Invoiced immediately.
   - Quickest to approve (Procurement sign-off only).

2) Surge buffer credit (pre-purchase credits)
   - You purchase a buffer at a reduced blended rate; unused credit rolls forward for 90 days.
   - Soft discount versus list; avoids a large single invoice if usage cools.

3) Early annualization (co-term and reprice)
   - Annualize now to lock a larger commit at a better blended discount; we pro-rate to co-term with your existing anniversary.
   - Requires PO + legal amendment (DocuSign). Better unit economics over time.

4) True-up at next invoice + smoothing note
   - We invoice actuals at month end but can add a billing note to split the hit across 2 invoices (if agreed in Procurement).
   - Useful if you expect the spike to be transient.

Key trade-offs: speed vs economics. Top-up is fastest; annualization gives best rates but takes longer. If you want, we can draft a short amendment (we’ve prepared templates) and surface a blended annualization example for your numbers.

Next steps: send over the usage CSV (I attached the stubbed version you shared), confirm whether Procurement wants a one-off PO or prefers an amendment, and I’ll loop in Marissa for pricing and Ben for finance approval. Happy to set a 30m call tomorrow.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage_report_Q2-2027.csv (CSV, 28KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: pricing proposal for BrightWave surge

Folks — quick internal note after looking at the usage file and Alex's ask. My recommended path (fastest + protective):
- Offer a 30-day buffer credit equivalent to 150% of current committed usage at a 10% blended discount vs list. Credit usable for 90 days.
- In parallel, offer an optional annualization illustration: if they convert the buffer into a 12-month commit today, they’d move to a 15% blended discount and we’d pro-rate the remainder of the current term. Attach amendment draft for procurement.

Why this combo: gives BrightWave immediate headroom, reduces invoice shock, and creates a clear upgrade path to better economics. Finance is OK with the 10% buffer discount for pre-pays; anything deeper requires approval from RevOps (Marissa).

Marissa — can you weigh in on approval and whether we can present a two-line DocuSign amendment (buffer credit then co-term option) to reduce legal friction? If yes I’ll produce numbers and a short commercial term sheet for Alex.

- Ben

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Harper <alex@brightwave.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike — options for mid-cycle billing?

Alex / Procurement — thanks for the patience. We modeled three clean paths and attached a short amendment draft you can circulate internally. Summary below:

A) 30-day Buffer Credit (recommended fast path)
- What: Pre-purchase buffer equal to 1.5x current committed monthly usage.
- Price: blended unit price with 10% off list.
- Term & use: Credit expires in 90 days; unused credit carries as one-time offset on next invoice.
- Approval: PO from Procurement.

B) Convert to Annual Commit (better economics)
- What: Convert buffer into a 12-month committed amount today.
- Price: blended 15% discount; pro-rate to co-term with your existing anniversary.
- Approval: PO + DocuSign amendment (link below).

C) True-up option (conservative)
- What: Bill actuals at month end; we can split the invoice across two billing periods to smooth cashflow.
- Price: list rates for the overage; no change to committed-tier discounts.

Attached: amendment_draft_3.pdf (PDF, 120KB) — includes two DocuSign-ready paths (Buffer Credit or Annualize). Also attached the usage CSV for your review.

If Procurement wants, I can convert the buffer numbers into a one-page commercial summary for your finance team. Ready to schedule a 20m call tomorrow at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: amendment_draft_3.pdf (PDF, 120KB), usage_report_Q2-2027.csv (CSV, 28KB)
